instruction: Find the Google Translate extension in the Chrome Web Store and open its detail page.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent read plugin list document, switched to Chrome, navigated to Chrome Web Store, searched for 'Zoom Chrome Extension', found and opened its detail page, clicked 'Add to Chrome', but installation was blocked with 'Installation is not enabled' error. Agent stayed on the Zoom extension page for remaining turns, never attempted other plugins.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can read documents in LibreOffice Writer, switch between applications, navigate to Chrome Web Store, search for extensions by name, click on search results to open extension detail pages, interact with 'Add to Chrome' button and permission dialogs
metadata.failure_analysis: Extension installation is disabled in the VM environment. The model got stuck after the first 'Installation is not enabled' error on Zoom Chrome Extension and did not attempt any of the other 4 plugins. The model lacked error recovery strategy.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original multi-plugin installation task into a single navigation task. Model demonstrated it can search and navigate to extension pages. This variation tests finding Google Translate extension page without requiring installation.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating from the initial LibreOffice Writer view to Chrome Web Store and finding the Google Translate extension detail page. Evaluator checks the active tab URL matches the Google Translate extension detail page pattern using regex.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'get_active_url_from_accessTree' correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL from the accessibility tree, which is exactly what's needed to verify the instruction.
Metric 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' correctly receives the URL string and checks it against the regex pattern list in rules['expected'].
Expected regex pattern 'chromewebstore\.google\.com/detail/google-translate' correctly matches the Google Translate extension detail page URL on Chrome Web Store.
Data flow is correct: get_rule returns the rules dict directly, metric accesses rules['expected'] to get the pattern list — no parameter handling issues.
Single instruction requirement (open the detail page) is fully covered by checking the active tab URL.
